chunks: When Our clear revelations are read out to them, the infidels say of the truth, when it has come to them: 'This is pure magic.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the disbelievers call the Quran clear magic?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights the cognitive dissonance of the disbelievers who, despite witnessing clear proofs (bayyinat), attribute the Quran's eloquence to 'clear magic' (sihr mubin) to preserve their pride. This dismissal reflects a deeper spiritual blindness where the miraculous nature of the text is rejected not due to lack of evidence, but due to obstinate rejection of the truth (haqq). The term 'sihr mubin' underscores that their accusation itself is a transparent falsehood, mirroring the Quran's own clarity.
